terms.comment: An inn or tavern (Lewis & Short); the landlord is caupō. We use it for a restaurant too (see restaurant).
A cook-shop where one ate and drank (Plaut.; Cic. Phil. 2.69; Hor.) (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Inv. 2.14: cum in eandem tabernam dēvertissent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Any shop or stall; a tavern where the context or an adjective says so, as taberna dēversōria (Plaut. Men. 2.3.81) (Lewis & Short).
pōtōrius is post-Augustan, of drinking vessels (Lewis & Short).

phrases.english: there’s drinking and eating, as if in a pub

phrases.latin: Unde nōbīs prōdīs? Ē popīnā quāpiam?
phrases.english: Where have you sprung from? Some pub?

sources: Lewis & Short: caupona · Lewis & Short: popina · Lewis & Short: taberna
